testPolicy.text: First-year applicants are required to submit SAT or ACT scores (self-reporting allowed; SAT and ACT superscored; ACT Science not required). Transfer applicants do not need scores.

cost.totalIncludes: Endowed colleges (and contract colleges for non-New York residents): tuition 73,946 + mandatory fees 1,024 (student activity 424 + Cornell Health 600) + housing 13,744 + food 7,604 (billed 96,318) + books and course materials 1,234 + personal 2,182. Transportation varies and is not in the total; Student Health Plan not included. New York residents in the NY State contract colleges: tuition 49,816, total 75,604.

aidPromise.text: Cornell meets 100 percent of demonstrated financial need for all eligible undergraduates. Most families with total annual income up to $75,000 and typical assets get $0 expected student and parent contributions and no student loans (grant aid plus a $5,000 work-study award). Above $75,000, aid offers include low loans capped at $2,000 ($75,001 to $125,000), $4,000 ($125,001 to $175,000) or $6,000 (above $175,000). These initiatives apply regardless of state residency or citizenship.

facts.text: New York residents pay much less in Cornell's NY State contract colleges and schools (Agriculture and Life Sciences, Dyson School, Human Ecology, ILR, and Brooks School BS programs): 2026-27 tuition is $49,816 instead of $73,946.
New York applicants were admitted at a much higher rate for fall 2025: 1,720 of 12,978 (13.3%), against 3,693 of 40,979 other US applicants (9.0%) and 664 of 18,566 international applicants (3.6%).
Early Decision is a big lever: 1,889 of 10,057 Early Decision applicants were admitted for fall 2025 (18.8%), against 4,188 of the other 62,466 applicants (6.7%); ED filled 31% of the admitted class.
Students apply to one specific undergraduate college or school at Cornell, each with its own requirements and selectivity.
Unlike most Ivy League peers, Cornell still packages student loans above $75,000 of family income, capped at $2,000 to $6,000 a year depending on income.
Cornell's waiting list is large: 9,720 applicants were offered a place for fall 2025, 6,598 accepted and 254 were admitted.

notes: The CDS PDF (https://irp.cornell.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Cornell-Common-Data-Set-2025-26.pdf) uses form fields that pypdf cannot read, so figures were read from the official Excel version (CDS-C sheet and Answer Sheet; the Answer Sheet misaligns C21, so ED counts were taken from the CDS-C form: 10,057 applications, 1,889 admitted). The fall 2025 SAT/ACT submission rates (43%/13%) are low because that class applied before the current requirement; testPolicy.since null because the policy page gives no start date (web search quota exhausted, announcement not located). The finaid cost page shows three 2026-27 tabs (endowed, contract non-NY, contract NY) though a heading also says 2025-26; the 2026-27 tuition 73,946 matches CDS G1 for 2026-27. cost.contractCollegeNyResident is an extra field for the NY resident contract-college rate. Contract-college list per the cost page: CALS, Dyson School, Human Ecology, ILR, Brooks School BS candidates. No Class of 2030 official counts found. Accessed 2026-10-13.
